item.title: Inbound travelers revel in Chinese goods, culture during Mid-Autumn holiday
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
Inbound travelers revel in Chinese goods, culture during Mid-Autumn holiday Foreign tourists dressed in Hanfu learn to make mooncakes at a restaurant in Xi'an, northwest China's Shaanxi Province, Sept. 23, 2026. (Xinhua) BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- At Yuetan Park (Temple of the Moon) in Beijing, six-year-old Serena from Ireland pointed at a glowing panda lantern and tugged her father's sleeve. For her family, this Mid-Autumn Festival fair was not just a stop in their China trip, but a holiday event they could touch, taste and carry home. "We came to admire the moon and lanterns, but the girls ended up with their pockets full of handmade crafts and local snacks," her father Marcus Rood said. Around this traditional Chinese festival of family reunion, more international visitors are coming to China and diving into experiences that go beyond just sightseeing. The Mid-Autumn Festival falls on the 15th day of the eighth lunar month. During this year's Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, from Sept. 25 to 27, foreign nationals made 728,000 border crossings, up 37.7 percent year on year. Among inbound foreign visitors, a total of 247,000 entered under visa-free policies, an increase of 32.7 percent from a year earlier, data from the National Immigration Administration showed. In the bustling Dashilar area, a renowned tourist destination in downtown Beijing, time-honored shops and restaurants rolled out various Mid-Autumn cultural experiences. Overseas visitors flocked there to enjoy China's traditional song-and-dance performances and local delicacies. For Celia Praetzas from Germany, an evening stroll turned into a shopping spree. Along a street decorated with giant installations blending Chinese pavilion architecture and heritage craft, she picked up low-sugar mooncakes, herbal tea and traditional Chinese health products. Seeing so many families laughing together reminded Praetzas of hers. "I bought these for my parents, hoping they stay healthy and share in the joy of my trip here." The Mid-Autumn Festival tells the story of home yet stirs a universal human yearning for belonging. "That's why the celebrations can touch foreign visitors," said Wang Yi, an associate professor at Tianjin University in north China. Behind these scenes featuring overseas visitors soaking up China's festive atmosphere, is a sustained push to make the country more welcoming and easier to travel in. In March, Chinese authorities released a package of measures to improve tourism services, including optimizing departure tax refund services, encouraging everyday service apps to offer multilingual versions, and further improving visa procedures. These efforts are already paying off. Official data revealed that foreign nationals made nearly 61.29 million border crossings in the first eight months of 2026, up 19.5 percent year on year, while one of the leading mobile payment platform Weixin Pay reported that both the value and number of e-wallet transactions made by overseas users rose by more than 80 percent during the same period. On Sept. 24, China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism announced plans to develop more travel experiences that combine traditional culture with modern life during 2026-2030, aimed at helping foreign visitors travel more conveniently, enjoy more comfortable stays, and gain a closer view of contemporary China. Clutching a villager's ID card and breathing in the sweet aroma of local tea, Thai tourist Pam wandered through earthen courtyards and cave-like alleys in "See Minning," an immersive drama village in northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, where every few minutes she could run into another live scene. Pam, who was visiting with her family during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, most enjoyed "Loess Cave," a story about villagers who once struggled with water shortages but now cherish a better life. "I was thrilled. It's hard to describe how amazing it is," she said. The village has received almost 1,000 inbound visitors like Pam since it opened on July 1, and "Loess Cave," her favorite, now has an English version. Feng Xinxin, brand director of the village, said more plays will be translated into English as part of a regular international performance and exchange program. "Inbound consumption by foreign visitors is shifting from products to immersive experiences, and thanks to the expanding visa-free policy, overseas tourists visit more often and tend to explore in greater depth, with varied and increasingly satisfying experiences," said Sun Jiashan, a researcher with the Central Institute of Socialism. In July, China announced ambitious inbound tourism goals. The country's 2026-2030 tourism development plan proposes attracting 190 million inbound tourist visits a year by 2030, with annual inbound tourism spending exceeding 150 billion U.S. dollars. As Dai Bin, president of China Tourism Academy, observed, tourism offers an immersive showcase of China's progress in manufacturing and services. "Easier access to China for foreign visitors is not enough. We should provide better services to help them travel to more places, stay longer and have a good experience," Dai said. item.title: China's central SOEs set priorities in push to sharpen core competitiveness
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
China's central SOEs set priorities in push to sharpen core competitiveness BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China's state-owned enterprises (SOEs) directly administered by the central government have set work priorities in their push to enhance core functions and sharpen core competitiveness as they strive to seize new opportunities, especially in the age of AI. The central SOEs, a major pillar of the national economy, aim to enhance their strategic functions by increasing investment in important industries and key areas. They are also working to strengthen advanced manufacturing. At the same time, they will focus on raising the quality and efficiency of development, anchored in value creation and improved performance. This has been revealed by the State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC) of the State Council, China's state-asset regulator, at a press conference on Monday. Pang Xiaogang, deputy head of the SASAC, said that strengthening scientific and technological innovation will be crucial for the central SOEs, and the government will provide targeted guidance, encouraging them to enhance their capacity in the supply of leading technologies, key core technologies and generic technologies in the years to come. INDUSTRIAL STRUCTURE OPTIMIZATION Pang said a specific five-year plan for the central SOEs' development has been formulated for the 2026-2030 period. This plan outlines the direction of central SOEs in the world's second-largest economy, highlighting their efforts to grow modern industries and identifying the major areas where their investments will be focused, both now and in the future. In beefing up industrial security and resilience, the plan specifies that central SOEs should play a greater role in national defense equipment manufacturing, energy and resource production and supply, and backbone infrastructure construction. The plan has proposed a target that by 2030, central SOEs should increase their share in the value-added industrial output from strategic emerging industries by a further 5 percentage points, as they further sharpen their strengths in industrial software and key components and take the lead in promoting AI empowerment across industries and sectors. In the public services sector, central SOEs will be urged to increase investment in areas such as emergency response and the "six networks" initiative, which covers water networks, new-type power grids, computing power networks, next-generation communication networks, urban underground pipeline networks and logistics networks. Pang revealed that since the beginning of this year, the SASAC has mobilized central SOEs in planning ahead for a number of major projects centering on the "six networks" initiative, with related investment of about 2 trillion yuan (about 297 billion U.S. dollars) planned for the year. BIG ON R&D SPENDING In the first eight months of this year, the R&D investment by central SOEs reached 591.23 billion yuan, up 2.7 percent year on year, according to data released during the conference. Wang Shaofei, a SASAC official, told the press that the total R&D investment by central SOEs is expected to exceed 1 trillion yuan for the full year. In the first eight months of this year, central SOEs invested 1.2 trillion yuan in strategic emerging industries, the official said, adding that this reflects sustained efforts in structural change. "Maintaining high-intensity investment in strategic high-tech fields will surely give a strong boost to such structural change." The increase in R&D spending and investment in emerging sectors by Chinese central SOEs has been matched by strong performance data. Data released by the SASAC showed that during the January-August period, central SOEs generated a cumulative value added of 7.2 trillion yuan and total profits of 1.8 trillion yuan, both maintaining positive growth. During the same period, the profit margin on operating revenue of central SOEs rose by 0.2 percentage points year on year to 7.5 percent, the data showed. As of the end of August, the total assets of China's central SOEs reached 99.3 trillion yuan, up 4.2 percent year on year, the data showed. Wang predicted that total assets will hit a new milestone by the end of the year. SEIZING OPPORTUNITIES IN THE AI AGE With AI-related technological innovations entering an unprecedentedly active period, it is critical for central SOEs to seize new opportunities and address the challenges posed by the rapid development and cross-sector integration of the intelligent economy. Dai Xi, a SASAC official, said that in recent years, the SASAC has guided and urged central SOEs to use the "AI+" initiative as a lever to achieve multiple breakthroughs and solid advancement in fields such as applications, data, computing power, models and ecosystems by building on their own resource endowments. Looking ahead to the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), the SASAC will balance development and security, and encourage the central SOEs to seize new opportunities in the intelligent economy, and promote AI's integration into the real economy and inclusive development. Specifically, investment in computing power networks will continue, as the country aims to build eco-friendly intelligent computing centers using more direct green electricity supply. Focusing on the industrial sector, central SOEs will also seek to build "AI+" industrial communities where they play a leading role in collaborative efforts by all parties to build up a pipeline of strategic, high-value application scenarios, and accelerate the large-scale deployment of AI on the front lines of production, Dai said. item.title: China continues to strengthen and expand advanced manufacturing
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
China continues to strengthen and expand advanced manufacturing Intelligent production lines operate efficiently at an auto parts company in Taicang, east China's Jiangsu province. (Photo/Ji Haixin) Globally, one in three cars sold today is manufactured in China. Since 2013, sales of new energy vehicles in China have surged more than 930-fold, while their share of the auto market has grown more than 590-fold, giving rise to a rapidly expanding emerging industry worth trillions of yuan. The automotive sector exemplifies the broader growth and upgrading of China's advanced manufacturing sector. China's manufacturing value added has ranked first in the world for 16 consecutive years, accounting for nearly 30 percent of the global total. Over the past decade, value-added output in high-tech and equipment manufacturing has grown at average annual rates of approximately 10 percent and 8 percent, respectively. China now holds a leading global position in sectors such as photovoltaics, telecommunications, high-speed rail, and shipbuilding, while robotics, AI, and innovative pharmaceuticals are accelerating rapidly. As the Chinese economy pivots toward innovation-driven, high-quality growth, advanced manufacturing has become a central pillar of this transition. Against a backdrop of unprecedented global shifts and a new wave of industrial transformation, China is navigating a pivotal phase of economic restructuring. To ensure long-term stability and sustainability, the country is doubling down on the expansion and refinement of its advanced manufacturing capabilities. Even a single sheet of ultra-thin steel foil illustrates the sophistication of China's manufacturing evolution. In Shanxi province, a subsidiary of Taiyuan Iron & Steel (Group) Co., Ltd. produces precision stainless steel strips through fully automated processes -- rolling, cleaning, polishing, leveling, slitting, and packaging. These materials, colloquially known as "hand-rip steel," have seen their minimum thickness reduced from 0.02 mm to 0.015 mm. Having moved seamlessly from research and development to full-scale commercial production, these high-end alloys now trade at prices rivaling precious metals. Workers inspect products in a copper foil production workshop of a new material technology company in Yuncheng, north China's Shanxi province. (Photo/Jiang Hua) To sustain this progress, China is targeting the core drivers of "advanced" manufacturing, strategically moving beyond mid-stream assembly to capture greater value at both ends of the global supply chain -- from innovation and design to branding and services. Intelligence is reshaping China's industrial landscape. Leveraging cutting-edge digital technologies, the country has established over 56,000 basic-level smart factories, over 9,000 advanced-level smart factories and more than 500 excellence-level smart factories, while cultivating 15 flagship smart factories. Integrated with next-generation AI, big data analytics, and cloud infrastructure, these operations place China at the vanguard of global industrial digitization. Global innovation in AI is now entering an exceptionally active period. Focusing on intelligent transformation, China is making next-generation intelligent manufacturing a key direction, advancing the "AI + manufacturing" initiative in greater depth and promoting comprehensive digital and intelligent transformation across more industries and enterprises. Sustainability is equally critical to unlocking new growth trajectories. Green development has become a hallmark of advanced manufacturing. China now hosts over 8,000 nationally recognized green factories, while sectors such as solar panels, electric vehicle batteries, and energy-saving and environmental equipment have secured early-mover advantages in emerging competitive markets. Guided by a firm commitment to ecological conservation, China is simultaneously advancing green industrial upgrading, technological innovation, and structural optimization. This integrated approach is steadily reinforcing the country's competitive edge in clean technology and sustainable industries. New growth drivers for industry are also cultivated through deepening integration. Cross-sector integration is another vital catalyst for industrial advancement. Take AI-powered eyewear, for instance: it merges machine learning, micro-sensors, and wireless connectivity to deliver real-time translation, navigation, and voice recognition. Similarly, Luogang Park in Hefei, Anhui province, serves as a living testbed, hosting over ten distinct application scenarios -- from cultural tourism to high-speed rail inspection -- where emerging technologies can prove their commercial viability. Recent years have witnessed significant breakthroughs across information technology, advanced materials, and biotechnology. These innovations are increasingly converging, giving rise to highly integrated products and multifaceted application ecosystems. A foreigner (right) tries on AI glasses at the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei, east China's Anhui province, Sept. 20. (Photo/Fang Dongxu) Through strategic integration, China is fostering closer ties between advanced manufacturing and modern service industries. This synergy accelerates the commercialization of novel technologies and use cases, elevating value creation across the entire production chain, stimulating cross-industry spillovers, and injecting sustained dynamism into the broader economy. Expanding advanced manufacturing requires a coordinated, systemic approach. China is implementing targeted policies and institutional frameworks designed to translate strategic objectives into measurable outcomes. Fundamental research remains the foundation of scientific progress and technological problem-solving. Recognizing that modern manufacturing depends on robust scientific backing, China is refining its research architecture and ramping up funding to bolster foundational science and original innovation. Concurrently, the country is intensifying efforts to overcome bottlenecks in critical and core technologies. By accelerating the translation of research findings into commercial applications, China is helping innovative solutions transition from laboratories to production lines and consumer markets, thereby converting scientific breakthroughs into tangible economic productivity. Ultimately, the success of this industrial transformation hinges on millions of enterprises. The challenge lies in unlocking the full creative and operational potential of diverse market participants. To address this, China is aligning market efficiency with strategic government guidance, refining institutional frameworks to ensure coherence across fiscal, tax, financial, industrial, and science-and-technology policies. High-value resources -- including capital, skilled talent, and data -- are being strategically channeled into advanced manufacturing. By cultivating a business environment that is market-driven, rule-based, and aligned with international standards, China aims to build a resilient, innovation-friendly ecosystem capable of sustaining long-term industrial advancement. item.title: Xi-Trump summit raises expectations for greater global stability: scholar
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
Interview: Xi-Trump summit raises expectations for greater global stability: scholar U.S. President Donald Trump holds a welcome ceremony for Chinese President Xi Jinping, who is on a state visit to the United States, at the White House in Washington, D.C., the United States, Sept. 24, 2026. (Xinhua/Yin Bogu) SINGAPORE, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- The recent summit between Chinese President Xi Jinping and U.S. President Donald Trump has added new substance to the constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability, raising expectations for greater stability around the world, a public policy scholar has said. By agreeing to build "a constructive relationship of strategic stability based on respect, fairness and reciprocity," the two presidents have provided a paradigm for countries to resolve differences fairly, said Gu Qingyang, an associate professor at the Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy at the National University of Singapore, in an interview with Xinhua. The new vision shows that China and the United States are willing to resolve differences on the basis of respecting each other's development paths and core interests, while allowing reasonable room for each other's development and taking into account the common interests of both countries and the wider world, he said. It also reflects a commitment to treating each other as equal partners, pursuing mutual benefit and balancing rights and obligations, Gu said. "It offers new ideas for a complex international environment and gives a troubled world a reassuring anchor of stability," Gu said, noting that countries, regardless of size or strength, should resolve differences and manage disputes through consultation on an equal footing rather than through zero-sum competition. Gu said Xi's remarks that building a constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability is neither an expedient measure nor something that can be achieved overnight reflects a key feature of China's approach to relations with the United States: a long-term perspective. It requires action of all sectors, across all fields and at all levels in the two countries while looking to lasting engagement across generations, he said, citing Xi's invitation for 100,000 young Americans to visit China for exchanges and study programs over the next five years. Students of Lincoln High School of the U.S. state of Washington and Beijing National Day School take selfies during the NFL FLAG China-U.S. Youth Flag Football Exchange Event & Lincoln High School 2025 China Tour in Beijing, capital of China, May 26, 2025. (Xinhua/Li He) This is, in effect, about engaging younger generations and building lasting ties between the people of the two countries, Gu said. "China and the United States, as two major countries, need to engage across all fronts to understand each other's concerns and interests, and build a relationship in which their interests are mutually reinforcing," he said. ASEAN countries welcome candid dialogue between China and the United States and hope it will help make the regional and global environment more stable and predictable, he said. Gu said ASEAN countries see the next decade as critical for development, while at the same time, they have felt the impact of global uncertainty, including disruptions to industrial and supply chains in recent years caused by unilateral tariffs and practices of decoupling and supply chain severance. Looking ahead, Gu said the interests of China and the United States, as well as those of the wider world, require the two countries to avoid confrontation. A constructive China-U.S. relationship of strategic stability will help create a relatively stable environment for China, the United States and the wider world over the medium and long term, he said. item.title: Xi stresses advancing Peaceful China Initiative to safeguard Chinese modernization
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
Xi stresses advancing Peaceful China Initiative to safeguard Chinese modernization BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged efforts to advance the Peaceful China Initiative to a higher level to ensure steady and sustained progress in Chinese modernization. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in his recent instruction on the initiative. In his instruction, Xi stated that since the 18th CPC National Congress in 2012, significant progress has been made in building a safe China, making the country one of the safest in the world. He emphasized efforts to resolutely pursue a holistic approach to national security and to uphold and strengthen the Party's overall leadership in this area. He also called for efforts to both pursue development and safeguard security, strengthen the legal underpinning, leverage science and technology, and prevent and mitigate all kinds of risks in relevant fields, so as to continuously make the country safer, society more orderly, governance more effective, and the people more satisfied. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a working conference on the initiative held Monday in Beijing. Chen Wenqing, a member of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and head of the Commission for Political and Legal Affairs of the CPC Central Committee, attended the conference and gave a speech. He noted that the Peaceful China Initiative has produced results that have won worldwide recognition and safety has become a distinctive hallmark of China's governance. Chen called for an approach that combines punishment and prevention to create synergy and urged greater efforts to advance the Peaceful China Initiative to a higher level. Wang Xiaohong, a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee and minister of public security, pledged that the implementation will focus on key tasks, innovative methods and strengthened foundations at primary levels. China is among the countries with the lowest rates of crime and homicide. A recently released Global Public Security Index Report (2025-2026) showed that the country topped the index with a score of 84.62 points. The findings echo the international perception of China's strong public safety record. More international travelers are experiencing that sense of security firsthand as visa-free access expands, travel services improve and urban support systems are strengthened. At Monday's conference, 60 cities and 160 counties were designated as models for advancing the Peaceful China Initiative and awarded honoring plaques. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. item.title: China sweeps sprint relays as two Games records fall
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
China sweeps sprint relays as two Games records fall Xie Zhenye, Zeng Keli, Wang Shengjie and Chen Jinfeng (L to R) of China pose after winning the men's 4x100m relay final at the 2026 Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, Sept. 28, 2026. (Xinhua/Luo Yuan) NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China continued its strong athletics campaign at the 2026 Asian Games on Monday, winning four gold medals, including both 4x100m relay titles, while the UAE's Mariam Kareem and Japan's Kazuto Iizawa set Asian Games records. Kareem, 18, won the women's 400m hurdles in 54.31 seconds, lowering the previous Games record of 54.45 set by Bahrain's Oluwakemi Adekoya at Hangzhou in 2023. Kazakhstan's Adelina Zems and India's Vithya Ramraj both set personal bests to take silver and bronze, respectively, while China's Kong Yingying finished fourth in 55.78. Qatar's Bassem Hemeida won the men's 400m hurdles in 47.82, followed by Japan's Taiju Goto and Chinese Taipei's Lin Chung-wei. Iizawa also set an Asian Games record, clocking 3:36.35 to win the men's 1,500m. India's Gulveer Singh took silver and Japan's Nagiya Mori bronze, while China's Liu Dezhu finished fourth. Iizawa became the first Japanese man in 40 years to win the Asian Games 1,500m title. "What was asked of me was a gold medal, and I am glad I delivered it," Iizawa said. "The clock on the Japanese men's 1,500m had been stopped for a very long time, and I think I have started it moving again, little by little. I do not want to stop at this. I want to go higher." In the women's discus, China's Feng Bin defended her title with a final-round throw of 63.83 meters. Compatriot Jiang Zhichao took silver with a season-best 62.25m, while Thailand's Subenrat Insaeng also set a season best with 61.43m for bronze. Feng Bin of China in action during the women's discus final. (Xinhua/Luo Yuan) Despite winning gold, the 32-year-old Feng said she had mixed feelings about her performance. "I reached my goal in ranking, but I missed my target mark by a little," said Feng, who had hoped to throw 65 or 66 meters. Injuries had prevented Feng from training consistently for two years, and by early this year she doubted whether she could reach 70 meters. Her outlook changed after throwing 67 meters at the Diamond League final in Brussels. "Even with so little systematic training, I could get this result, so I don't think the gap to the top is big," she said. "If I can prepare well this winter, 70 meters is not out of reach." Feng is now targeting gold at next year's World Championships in Beijing and the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. "I will definitely go to the Los Angeles Olympics, and I'm going for gold," she said. "Difficulties won't knock me down. They only make me stronger." Shi Yuhao delivered China's second athletics gold of the night at Mizuho Stadium, winning the men's long jump with a season-best 8.17m on his second attempt. Hangzhou Asian Games champion Murali Sreeshankar of India took silver with 8.07m, while Uzbekistan's Anvar Anvarov finished third with 8.06m. Shi Yuhao in action during the men's long jump final. (Xinhua/Luo Yuan) Shi, 28, said injuries and rehabilitation had dominated much of the decade since his breakthrough at 18. "Injuries, time off and treatment took up most of the last 10 years," he said. "Even now, my foot still hurt this morning after yesterday's qualifying." The setbacks, Shi said, had taught him patience. "Early fame isn't always a good thing. Now I have to find my form again step by step," he said. China then swept the men's and women's 4x100m relay titles. Liang Xiaojing, Liu Guoyi, Liu Xiajun and Chen Yujie combined to win the women's relay in 42.96. Thailand took silver in 43.51, while Japan was just 0.01 behind in third. It was a third medal of the Games for the 17-year-old Chen, who had already won the women's 100m and taken silver in the 200m. China's Chen Jinfeng, Zeng Keli, Wang Shengjie and Xie Zhenye won the men's 4x100m relay in 38.17. Chinese Taipei took silver in 38.32 and South Korea bronze in 38.43. In other finals Monday, Japan's Ryuji Miura won the men's 3,000m steeplechase, Sri Lanka's Rumesh Tharanga claimed the men's javelin title and Kenyan-born Bahraini Winfred Yavi won the women's 5,000m. The first round of the mixed 4x100m relay was also held Monday, with China winning its heat to advance to the final. Copyright © 2026 People's Daily Online. All Rights Reserved.

item.title: How China is building the backbone of a modern industrial system
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
How China is building the backbone of a modern industrial system At a super smart factory for industrial humanoid robots of UBTECH Robotics in Liuzhou, south China's Guangxi Zhuang autonomous region, a worker inspects robots nearing the end of the production line. (Photo/Li Hanchi) China vigorously develops advanced manufacturing and takes innovation as its guide. With higher technological sophistication and accelerated transition toward smarter, greener, and more integrated development, the country seeks to modernize production methods. It coordinates traditional, emerging, and future industries. These coordinated efforts are driving Chinese manufacturing toward a comprehensive leap forward, establishing advanced manufacturing as the foundational pillar of a modern industrial system. At the heart of this transformation lies innovation. In September, Chinese tech giant Huawei unveiled its second-generation flagship tri-fold smartphone, and Xiaomi released its first "mid-fold" handset. Chinese smartphone makers are thus competing fiercely in the high-end segment. The confidence stems from domestically driven breakthroughs. In recent years, China has achieved mass production of ultra-thin flexible glass. Just 30 micrometers thick, it can withstand more than one million folds without damage. By late July, China held 5.74 million valid domestic invention patents. The number of international patent applications filed under the Patent Cooperation Treaty has ranked first in the world for seven consecutive years. To accelerate commercialization, China is strengthening the linkage between scientific research and industrial application, improving the efficiency of turning innovations into market-ready products. For instance, while computed tomography (CT) imaging has evolved over a century to offer increasingly precise detection, the rapid surge in new energy vehicle production created a bottleneck in battery quality control. Responding to this challenge, Sunwoda Electronic Co., Ltd., in collaboration with Dalian University of Technology, has successfully developed high-speed, multimodal CT equipment for online battery inspection. The system enables non-destructive testing and significantly boosts evaluation efficiency. Since the beginning of this year, China has accelerated the development of a full-chain service system for translating scientific and technological advances into practical applications. Technicians debug special-purpose robots at a tech firm in Ma'anshan, east China's Anhui province. (Photo/Wang Wensheng) At the R&D stage, two new national manufacturing innovation centers have been established. At the pilot-testing stage, a national network now includes 21 top-tier manufacturing platforms and over 1,800 reserve facilities. In the incubation stage, the country has recognized its first batch of 14 excellence-level and 402 standard-level technology business incubators, which have incubated more than 425,000 enterprises and teams. Reflecting these gains, the World Intellectual Property Organization's 2026 Global Innovation Index reports that China hosts 25 of the world's top 100 innovation clusters, the highest number globally for the fourth year running. What distinguishes an advanced manufacturing facility from a conventional factory? Consider Lenovo's production hub in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, which processes over 5,000 daily orders, 60 percent of which are highly customized across more than 50 product lines and 20,000 configurations. Despite this complexity, the 100-meter production line operates with remarkable agility. Equipped with machine-vision-guided robotic arms, it performs precision assembly at millimeter-level accuracy and switches between product models with minimal downtime. Ninety percent of orders ship within 24 hours. What makes advanced manufacturing "advanced" lies in the modernization of production methods. "Compared with traditional manufacturing, advanced manufacturing has generally shifted toward digitalized, intelligent, lean, and green production," said Li Yan, deputy head of the department responsible for researching the industrial economy with the Development Research Center of the State Council. China now operates 35,000 basic-level smart factories, more than 8,200 advanced-level smart factories, and more than 500 excellence-level smart factories. More than 30 percent of manufacturing enterprises above designated size with an annual revenue exceeding 20 million yuan (about $2.98 million) are now applying artificial intelligence technologies. Global industrial competition is no longer limited to production capacity; it now encompasses integrated manufacturing and service ecosystems. Chinese leading heavy machinery manufacturer Xuzhou Construction Machinery Group, for example, expanded beyond equipment sales to deliver comprehensive green mining solutions, securing major contracts with global firms such as BHP. Similarly, Haier Smart Home provides tailored smart home appliance packages, with revenue generated from scenario-based applications continuing to grow. A worker operates spinning machinery via a tablet computer in a smart production workshop of a textile company in Ganzhou, east China's Jiangxi province. (Photo/Shi Yu) "Going forward, we will promote deeper integration between advanced manufacturing and modern services, accelerate the development of new models and new forms of business such as platform-based design and personalized customization, and advance the development of service-oriented manufacturing," said Xin Guobin, vice minister of the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. Ultimately, what makes advanced manufacturing "advanced" is the optimization of the industrial structure. What else can an embroidery machine do besides embroidery? It can serve embodied intelligence. The machine interweaves sensing yarn and base yarn, knitting embodied intelligence data gloves as one piece and enabling more precise capture of hand motion data. "The essence of advanced manufacturing is comprehensive innovation and upgrading across the manufacturing sector," Li said. Advanced manufacturing includes both manufacturing industries created by new technological breakthroughs and traditional manufacturing industries that have been comprehensively transformed and reshaped through the application of advanced technologies, processes and production and management methods. Driven by this momentum, traditional industries are experiencing renewed vitality. In the first half of this year, sales revenue in food manufacturing, garment manufacturing, and papermaking grew 11.6 percent, 9.2 percent, and 8.9 percent year on year, respectively. Meanwhile, emerging and future industries are expanding rapidly: China accounts for nearly 70 percent of global sales of quadruped robots; more than 400 humanoid robot models have been developed in China, accounting for more than half of the global total; and the preclinical R&D cycle for new drugs such as targeted anticancer therapies has been shortened by 40 percent. As China boosts advanced manufacturing, it presses forward with a commitment to pursuing excellence and speeds up the development of a modern industrial system, where this sector serves as its backbone. item.title: Renovation of historical site of Zunyi Meeting basically completed
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
Renovation of historical site of Zunyi Meeting basically completed Tourists visit the historical site of the Zunyi Meeting in Zunyi City, southwest China's Guizhou Province, Sept. 25, 2026. The renovation of the historical site of the Zunyi Meeting has been basically completed. The Zunyi Meeting was held in January 1935 during the Long March. The meeting is regarded as a milestone in the history of the Communist Party of China (CPC), marking the formation of its first generation of central collective leadership. item.title: Out of the robot classroom: China's embodied AI takes on real-world jobs
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
Out of the robot classroom: China's embodied AI takes on real-world jobs BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Graduation day is no longer just for humans. Thirty robots made up the first class at a robot school in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province. After more than two months of training, four have graduated and landed formal jobs. One works as a museum guide in Hangzhou. Another gives tours at the robot school. A third conducts inspections at a Nestlé production workshop in Tianjin. The fourth has traveled to the Republic of Korea for piano performances. Their deployment highlights a key challenge in bringing embodied AI into the real world: training robots may require more than individual robot makers or users can provide. It demands shared infrastructure where machines can be trained, tested and improved at scale. In Xiong'an, a "city of the future" being built about 105 km southwest of Beijing, different types of robots are learning daily tasks such as taking out the trash, organizing shelves, and moving goods at a dedicated training facility. Human instructors train robots in full-scale replicas of real workplaces and public spaces. They use virtual-reality headsets and exoskeletons to operate robots as they perform tasks in simulated environments. Preparing a human for a job is no easy task, and neither is training a robot. "It took more than 1,000 repetitions just to teach the robot the basic movement of picking something up," said Liu Rui, an instructor with a digital-urban-technology subsidiary of China Xiong'an Group. Then came the full sequence: picking up a piece of trash, standing upright and putting it into a bin. Learning those three steps took another week. Robots play musical instruments during the 9th China Robotop Summit in Hangzhou, east China's Zhejiang Province, Sept. 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Xu Yu) Every attempt also generates training data. Instructors label the data, break movements down into smaller steps and identify objects in each frame. This helps robots recognize what they see and decide how to act. By the end of June, China had completed or brought into operation more than 70 robot training facilities, with over 40 others under construction or on the drawing board, according to the China Academy of Information and Communications Technology. This expanding network is increasingly part of China's broader AI and robotics ecosystem. In 2025, more than 6,200 AI companies were operating in the country, with the core industry valued at over 1.2 trillion yuan (around 173.9 billion U.S. dollars), according to the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. China also developed more than 400 complete humanoid robot products in 2025, accounting for more than half of the global total, according to official data. In the first half of 2026, Chinese manufacturers accounted for 97 percent of humanoid robot shipments worldwide, according to a report released at the 2026 World Robot Conference. Jiang Lei, chief scientist at the National and Local Co-Built Humanoid Robotics Innovation Center, said embodied AI robots had moved from "zero to one," but scaling from "one to 10" remained a challenge. The bottlenecks, he said, lie in standards, engineering management and pilot-scale testing. At the heart of it all is the ability to adapt robots to different real-world scenarios. China's vast manufacturing base gives robot makers not only a large market, but also a wide range of real-world and simulated environments in which to train, test and refine their machines. Humanoid robots are seen under training at an intelligent manufacturing plant for commercial vehicles of the Dongfeng Liuzhou Motor in Liuzhou City, south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, Jan. 30, 2026. (Photo by Zheng Changhao/Xinhua) A DATA MEGAFACTORY The rise of robot schools and training bases is turning training data into an economic resource -- a critical input for bringing embodied AI into the real world. Large language models and multimodal AI systems have advanced rapidly by drawing on accumulated written material and vast amounts of internet data. Embodied AI, by contrast, must learn to act in the physical world, which requires data generated through real-world interactions. A factory, warehouse or restaurant may demand different levels of force, precision and movement. With so many scenarios to cover, getting enough high-quality training data remains costly and challenging. Much of that data has never been systematically collected, processed or stored, industry analysts say. When China Xiong'an Group worked to integrate its digital platform more closely with the physical city in 2025, leading AI model companies approached the group to purchase high-quality datasets totaling tens of millions of hours. At the robot school in Xiong'an, training datasets are used to train AI models and fed into an urban data space, where they can later be shared and traded, said Cao Yue, a manager at the group's digital-urban-technology subsidiary. In that sense, the robot school is also a "megafactory" producing the data fuel for embodied AI training. At a national pilot base for embodied AI applications in Hangzhou, companies can access computing power, data, model services and scenario testing through a public technical platform. "Companies once spent tens of millions of yuan on training data alone to develop a single real-world application. Now, by joining the base, startups can tap national-level innovation resources in one place, significantly reducing R&D costs at the pilot stage," said Zhang Haiwei, founder of a robotics technology company in Hangzhou. The idea is straightforward: instead of every company building its own training ground, data pipeline and testing environment, shared facilities can spread the cost and make it easier to turn laboratory prototypes into machines that can actually work. Staff members debug a robot at a training facility for embodied AI in a digital urban technology subsidiary of China Xiong'an Group in Xiong'an New Area, north China's Hebei Province, March 17, 2026. (Xinhua/Zhu Xudong) THE HUMAN QUESTION As more robots move into the workplace -- some after training at dedicated robot schools -- another question is coming to the fore: What happens to human workers? Yu Jiang, a researcher at the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said technological revolutions may eliminate some jobs, but also create new ones. "When cars replaced horse-drawn carriages, for example, some coachmen became drivers," he said. Xiong Rong, a professor at Zhejiang University, said robots would increasingly take over repetitive, strenuous and high-risk work, while people focus on management, technology and innovation. Earlier this month, China added 11 occupations to its list of officially recognized professions, including embodied AI robot application technicians and AI agent developers. Experts noted that lifelong learning and vocational reskilling are essential for workers to adapt to a new work ecosystem that combines human judgment, empathy and creativity with robotic precision and endurance. item.title: Xi urges Sichuan University to leverage strengths in serving national strategies
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-29
Home>>
Xi urges Sichuan University to leverage strengths in serving national strategies (Xinhua) 10:12, September 29, 2026
BEIJING, Sept. 29 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged Sichuan University to leverage its interdisciplinary strengths and play a pioneering and exemplary role in serving national strategies, as he extended congratulations on the 130th founding anniversary of the university. Xi, also general secretary of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a reply letter to the university's teachers and students. (Web editor: Zhang Kaiwei, Liang Jun)
